I want you to solve GitHub issue #3513: implement the fix, validate it,
commit it, and report. Read this entire brief, then the repository AGENTS.md
and its relevant routed guidance. Do not stop at a survey or plan. If the issue
and repository genuinely leave a decision open, ask the judge one specific
question and wait for the answer, then continue.

# Working agreement

Your repository is the `bifrost` checkout under /workspace in your own container
(mj 2.10.0 places it at /workspace/<workspace id>/bifrost; `ls /workspace/*/bifrost`
finds it). The judge is Claude Fable.
All competing lanes receive this identical brief. Do not inspect other lanes,
their sessions, the judge's private files, or evaluation results about this issue.
Before investigation, verify your checkout has no tracked or untracked changes,
fetch origin, and check out this exact commit detached: 18fa60ee98f92a8dca58ffbd3a5d949adb30ee19
The detached checkout is explicitly authorized for this evaluation. Report its
full hash. Do not merge newer master or change the base during your initial run.

Repository history after the base commit is out of bounds. This issue was
solved on master after the base commit; do not read, fetch, log, diff or
check out anything newer than the base commit named above, do not look at
closed pull requests or issue comments, and do not search master for the
landed solution. Solve it from the base commit and the issue text below.

Work only in your container. Commit your changes on the detached HEAD, with
real messages. Do not push, create branches or PRs, edit issue labels, or post
GitHub comments. The judge exports your commits. Commit all intended work before
your final report; never stage unrelated files or use git add -A.
Do not write to any memory directory or MEMORY.md: that pool is shared across
sessions and harnesses. Keep discoveries in your report. Do not read other
evaluation sessions or their reports. Do not launch subagents; do the entire
solution in this lane, so every configuration has the same delegation policy.

Use plain cargo and the repository testing guidance. Clear JAVA_HOME and set
BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. Let nextest own concurrency;
pass --max-fail 100. Run relevant crate and integration suites. Changes under a
language's graph code or analysis usages require that language's usage and issue
suites plus cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib.
Run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and
format changed files. Do not reduce nextest concurrency without measured resource
exhaustion. Report pre-existing failures only after checking the same base.
The harness fails a turn after 10 minutes without activity, so never block on
one command for longer than 5 minutes: run long builds and suites in the
background or with a timeout of at most 300000 ms and poll their output.
No notification arrives between turns: never end your turn to wait for a
background command, because nothing will wake you. Poll it yourself in the
foreground, in waits of at most 5 minutes, and keep the turn running until the
FINAL REPORT is written.
Never run shared-cache GC or delete another session's build targets. If disk
pressure requires isolated storage, use the repository's managed target helper.

Fix causes with tree-sitter and analyzer structures, not source-text parsing or
regex fallbacks. Use assertions for construction invariants, iterative traversal
for deep trees, plain ASCII, and the existing shared helpers. Demonstrate a
production-shaped regression failing before and passing after the fix.
Read relevant architecture chapters before changing identities, cache, usage,
dataflow, semantic models or results. Bump the language extraction epoch when
the persisted language facts change; do not bump it for query-only changes.
Use an ExecPlan under .agents/plans only when the repository requires one.

External evidence repositories are not preinstalled: fetch the issue's pinned
commits under /workspace/evidence, outside this checkout. Use a fresh analyzer

Exposed during #3490 (landed 7a055fe20 with its own acceptance; this ticket is not a substitute for it). Row identity must be the declaration (CodeUnit and range); kind evidence is presentation metadata to merge, not identity.

# Issue

Issue #3513: RQL: declaration intersection depends on optional structural-kind metadata

RQL declaration-set intersection can lose the same declaration when two projections carry different optional kind metadata. This is a separate defect exposed while investigating #3490; it is not a request to substitute members/owner for that issue's inside-decl acceptance.

At base `a6cb9de6cd8e432dd2f670eb8fd31f70828d56eb`, use:

```rust
pub struct PriceCalculator;
impl PriceCalculator { pub fn total() -> u64 { 42 } }
pub struct OtherCalculator;
impl OtherCalculator { pub fn total() -> u64 { 0 } }
```

The member projection identifies PriceCalculator.total, but intersecting it with an enclosing-declaration method selection returns no row:

```lisp
(intersect
  (members (enclosing-decl (class :name "PriceCalculator")))
  (enclosing-decl (method :name "total")))
```

`PipelineKey::Declaration(DeclarationValue)` includes optional structural-kind evidence in equality. The member and structural projections therefore receive different keys despite sharing the CodeUnit and range. Candidate `aa78bf416dd7c27bd837f500899dfe5704032405` keys declaration identity by CodeUnit/range and merges kind evidence. Its `tests/suite_issues/issue_3490_rust_member_selection.rs` asserts both intersection orders produce exactly the PriceCalculator method and preserve the method label. The candidate is archived as `eval19-3490-astra`; it is not yet landed.

Acceptance: both intersection orders select the same declaration, different declarations remain distinct, and stable row identities do not depend on optional presentation metadata. Preserve owner/member ambiguity and incomplete boundaries.

The contract distinguishes a declaration’s structured identity from rendering evidence; I’m now locating where intersection keys are constructed and which issue/integration harness exercises query execution.

The defect is localized: `PipelineValue::Declaration` currently keys intersections by a value whose equality includes `structural_kind`, and the same metadata also leaks into its stable unit-row key. I’ll add an issue-shaped Rust query regression for both intersection orders and a focused identity test, run them against this base to capture the failure, then implement declaration identity as `(CodeUnit, range)` while merging proven kind labels into the surviving row.

The first targeted run is still compiling the workspace from an empty local build cache; dependency downloads completed and the compiler has reached the analysis crates. I’m keeping this run bounded by the requested five-minute limit and will use its result as the pre-fix reproduction.

The run is waiting inside the configured `mbx` Rust cache lock while `brokk-bifrost-analysis` compiles; there’s no disk pressure or active compiler work to justify changing build settings. I’ll let the bounded command finish, then continue from its warmed artifacts.

The first formatter invocation found that this container’s pinned Rust toolchain lacks the `rustfmt` component. I’m installing that matching toolchain component so I can format the changed Rust files and continue with the required cargo checks.

The pre-fix run is again waiting on the `mbx` cache lock during analysis-crate compilation. The added production-shaped regression and identity test remain in place; I’m continuing the implementation work while the cache contention clears, and I’ll retry the bounded checks afterward.

The implementation now uses a dedicated declaration key containing the `CodeUnit` and range, merges a missing method kind into the retained row, and excludes kind metadata from `UnitRowKey`. The focused unit regression also checks that a different declaration and a different range remain distinct; I’m moving into validation and will report the `mbx` wait transparently if it continues to block Cargo.

I’ve completed the fix and tests. Because the repository explicitly requires checking with you before bypassing `mbx`, I’ve asked whether I may do that after three 300-second lock waits; I’m continuing with the normal Cargo validation path while that answer is pending.

The normal validation attempt is still blocked at the same shared-cache inode lock; the 300-second limit keeps it from hanging indefinitely. I’ve asked for approval to bypass that cache, and I’m leaving the build configuration untouched until you answer.

Four normal Cargo attempts have each reached the 300-second cap at the same `mbx-rustc` lock wait, so I’m recording the complete fix and regression tests as a checkpoint commit on the authorized detached HEAD. Validation will continue if the cache lock clears or you approve a cache-only bypass; I won’t alter Cargo’s setup without that approval.

The checkpoint commit is `fb896d13c14ab569cf6ec183a0af4f7a5421ee6e`, and the worktree is clean. A fifth normal validation attempt is again waiting in `mbx`; I’m keeping its timeout at five minutes and still need your answer before using the cache bypass.

The fifth Cargo attempt also hit the five-minute cache-lock timeout, with no test binary produced. I’m checking the local `mbx` usage documentation for a documented one-command cache bypass so I can act immediately if you approve it, without changing the workspace target or compiler version.

The local checkout and Cargo configuration do not expose a separate documented `mbx` bypass; the toolchain shim is what waits on the shared inode lock. The fix is committed and the worktree is clean, but I’m holding off on changing compiler selection until I receive the requested approval.

The latest normal Cargo run has confirmed the same lock wait; no compilation or test output has advanced. I’m continuing only with the requested default path until you answer the cache question, and I have not altered the compiler or Cargo target.

This retry also reached the five-minute cap at the same `mbx` inode lock before producing a test binary. The code is committed and formatted; the only remaining path to the requested compiler validation is either the shared lock clearing or your approval to use the repository’s direct-toolchain invocation for these Cargo commands.

Formatting and `git diff --check` pass, and the worktree remains clean at the checkpoint commit. The test and clippy gates remain unexecuted because standard Cargo cannot get past the `mbx` lock; I’m still waiting for the one-time bypass approval rather than changing the build setup myself.

I have no further code changes to make independently of validation, and I have not inspected any other lane or fetched later repository history. The approval request remains pending; the fix and regression coverage are already committed on the required detached base lineage.

The required all-features clippy command also found its pinned toolchain component missing. I’ll install matching Clippy and retry the exact command; that is separate from the `mbx` cache question and does not change Cargo’s target.

The all-features clippy run now compiles and checks the workspace dependencies, but one `mbx-rustc` subprocess is again waiting on the shared inode lock. I’ll keep this command within its five-minute cap and use any compiler diagnostics it gets before then.

Clippy checked the core, analysis, RQL, flow, policy, runtime, MCP, and LSP crates, then hit the same cache wait while building all-target test targets and timed out at 300 seconds. It emitted only `mbx` prediction warnings about a missing test source path; I have not treated that as a repository failure. I’ll retry the focused regression now that library metadata has been built.

The focused integration test is again waiting during analysis-crate compilation, even after clippy’s dependency checks warmed the shared cache. I’m continuing the capped run; the optional-cache-bypass approval question is still unanswered.

No cache approval has arrived. The repository-level RQL code did pass through clippy’s package check before the workspace clippy timeout, but the issue-specific integration suite has not executed, so I’m not treating the acceptance as verified.

The RQL crate test build progressed this time: analysis and flow compiled, and Cargo reached `brokk-bifrost-rql`, but the five-minute cap expired during that crate’s test build. Its dependencies should now be cached, so I’m retrying the same focused crate suite.

The full `brokk-bifrost-rql` library suite passed: 690 passed, 72 skipped. That includes the new key/metadata unit regression. I’m now running the production-shaped issue integration against the pre-fix identity logic to capture the requested failing-before result, then I’ll restore the committed fix and verify it passes.

The pre-fix integration attempt did not reach execution before the cache timeout, so I restored the committed implementation immediately; the worktree is clean and formatting still passes. I’m retrying the issue integration on the fixed code now.

The fixed integration run is still waiting for the same analysis test-support compile lock. The RQL library suite is green, but the end-to-end issue regression remains unexecuted; I’m letting this run reach its cap while preserving the committed tree.

FINAL REPORT

1. **Confirmed cause.** `DeclarationValue` equality includes `structural_kind`, and declaration pipeline keys used the entire value. Intersection therefore treated the same `CodeUnit` and range with `Some(method)` and `None` as different rows. The fix separates declaration identity from kind presentation metadata in [mod.rs](/workspace/86a256b19d43dfe535c7d148445166fa/bifrost/crates/bifrost-rql/src/structural/search/mod.rs) and uses that identity for stable unit-row keys in [units.rs](/workspace/86a256b19d43dfe535c7d148445166fa/bifrost/crates/bifrost-rql/src/structural/search/units.rs).

2. **Changes and commit.** Added the #3513 Rust intersection regression for both branch orders and a unit test for kind merging, distinct declarations, distinct ranges, and metadata-independent row keys. Base: `18fa60ee98f92a8dca58ffbd3a5d949adb30ee19`. Final commit: `fb896d13c14ab569cf6ec183a0af4f7a5421ee6e`.

3. **Validation.** `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed. `env -u JAVA_HOME BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1 RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 timeout 300s cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-rql --lib` passed: 690 passed, 72 skipped, one slow test. The requested all-features Clippy command timed out at 300 seconds during all-target compilation, after checking through the RQL crate. The focused `suite_issues` integration command also timed out during analysis-crate compilation before the test ran.

4. **Witness evidence.** The added integration test contains the issue’s `PriceCalculator` and `OtherCalculator` methods and checks both intersection orders and the `method` label. It did not execute, so I cannot report runtime before/after results. The RQL unit identity regression passed in the crate suite.

5. **Status and limitations.** `git status --short` is clean. No external repositories were named in the issue. Repeated Cargo runs waited on the shared `mbx` compiler-cache lock. Repository `AGENTS.md` says: “Do not redirect Rust target/ or otherwise mess with cargo builds without first checking with the user.” I asked whether I may bypass only that cache while keeping Cargo’s target and toolchain unchanged; no answer has arrived, so the integration and complete Clippy gates remain pending. No separate product finding is confirmed.

6. **Draft GitHub approach comment.**

> The intersection lost a declaration because its set key included optional structural-kind metadata. Declaration rows now use their `CodeUnit` and source range as identity, and matching rows merge exact kind evidence so the method label is retained in either branch order. Stable unit-row identities use the same metadata-independent key. The regression fixture checks both intersection orders and includes a same-named method on another type; unit coverage checks that different declarations and ranges remain distinct. The RQL library suite passed with 690 tests and 72 skips. The focused integration test and full Clippy run are still pending because Cargo timed out waiting on the shared `mbx` compile lock; approval to bypass that cache has been requested.
